title: Bissell Park multi-use pad grant endorsed
subtitle: Termite subsidy program, settlement boundary report, housing servicing grants, hospital pond purchase and staff association agreement also featured.
overview: Council's main item was the proposed Bissell Park multi-use pad in Elora. The preferred option, a refrigerated surface with a roof at an estimated $5.7 million, was defeated {{vote:m8}}. Council then endorsed a scaled-back refrigerated option without a roof, at an estimated $4 million {{vote:m9}}. That option is contingent on a provincial grant covering half the cost, and it includes $700,000 in the 2025 draft capital budget and a community fundraising effort. Staff will return to Council if the grant is unsuccessful.

Council also approved a Termite Management Subsidy Program {{vote:m10}}, authorized applications for two provincial housing-related servicing grants {{vote:m12}}, and received a report on recommended settlement area boundary expansions for information only {{vote:m11}}. A final boundary decision will come later.

After a closed session, Council approved buying the stormwater pond at 131 Fredrick Campbell Street, Fergus, from Groves Memorial Community Hospital {{vote:m3}}. It also approved a tentative agreement with the Centre Wellington Staff Association {{vote:m4}}. Council authorized a development charge deferral agreement for a company expansion {{vote:m6}}.

decisions.detail: Council endorsed Option 2, a refrigerated multi-use surface without a roof at about $4,000,000, contingent on a 50% provincial grant, with $700,000 in the 2025 draft capital budget and a community fundraising effort.
Council defeated the staff-recommended Option 3, a refrigerated surface with a roof at about $5,700,000 {{vote:m8}}.
Council approved the subsidy program with immediate effect and delegated administration to a staff review committee and the Treasurer.
Staff will apply for Housing-Enabling Core Servicing funding for Colborne Street reconstruction and for the second intake of the Housing-Enabling Water Systems Fund for South Fergus.
Council authorized an agreement to buy the stormwater management pond at 131 Fredrick Campbell Street, Fergus, from Groves Memorial Community Hospital.
Council approved the tentative agreement with the Centre Wellington Staff Association and directed staff to update the Memorandum of Agreement.
Council authorized a Development Charge Deferral Payment Agreement for a manufacturing expansion in Fergus.

debate: Delegates supporting the pad described it as a free, drop-in, all-ages space used year round, and said the current surface is worn and unsafe. A basketball club said every option includes basketball but that its biggest need is indoor space.

A resident delegate argued that a refrigerated rink conflicts with climate commitments, citing energy use and warmer winters. Another youth delegate said a hockey-focused rink could exclude newcomers and asked for more basketball courts and an indoor dome.

Some councillors worried about the $700,000 top-up before 2025 budget talks and about consultation with the equity and healthy communities committees. One suggested a roofed option without refrigeration. Others said the grant is a rare, one-time chance and that the project fits Council's strategic plan.

Staff said the grant intake favours early applications, that nothing proceeds without the grant, and that sustainability review could be added at design stage. The consultant said the roof would cut cooling demand.

On the settlement boundary, many landowner delegates asked for their lands to be added. Staff said the recommendation matches the approved land need and that adding land would exceed it or require removing other land.
